v: The vision[^1] of Obadiah.[^2] This is what the Lord Yahweh[^3] says concerning Edom:[^4] We have heard a report from Yahweh, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: "Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!"[^5]
חֲז֖וֹן עֹֽבַדְיָ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה לֶאֱד֗וֹם שְׁמוּעָ֨ה שָׁמַ֜עְנוּ מֵאֵ֤ת יְהוָה֙ וְצִיר֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם שֻׁלָּ֔ח ק֛וּמוּ וְנָק֥וּמָה עָלֶיהָ[c] לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
Look, I will make you small among the nations; you will be utterly despised.[^6]
הִנֵּ֥ה קָטֹ֛ן נְתַתִּ֖יךָ בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם בָּז֥וּי אַתָּ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃
The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock,[^7] whose dwelling is on the heights, who say in your heart, "Who will bring me down to the ground?"
זְד֤וֹן לִבְּךָ֙ הִשִּׁיאֶ֔ךָ שֹׁכְנִ֥י בְחַגְוֵי־סֶ֖לַע מְר֣וֹם שִׁבְתּ֑וֹ אֹמֵ֣ר בְּלִבּ֔וֹ מִ֥י יוֹרִדֵ֖נִי אָֽרֶץ׃
Though you build as high as the eagle,[^8] though your nest is set among the stars, from there I will bring you down, declares Yahweh.[^9]
אִם־תַּגְבִּ֣יהַּ כַּנֶּ֔שֶׁר וְאִם־בֵּ֥ין כּֽוֹכָבִ֖ים שִׂ֣ים קִנֶּ֑ךָ מִשָּׁ֥ם אוֹרִֽידְךָ֖ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
If thieves came to you, if robbers by night (how you will be destroyed!),[^10] would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape pickers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?
אִם־גַּנָּבִ֤ים בָּאֽוּ־לְךָ֙ אִם־שׁ֣וֹדְדֵי לַ֔יְלָה אֵ֣יךְ נִדְמֵ֔יתָה הֲל֥וֹא יִגְנְב֖וּ דַּיָּ֑ם אִם־בֹּֽצְרִים֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔ךְ הֲל֖וֹא יַשְׁאִ֥ירוּ עֹלֵלֽוֹת׃
How Esau[^11] has been searched out, his hidden treasures hunted down!
אֵ֚יךְ נֶחְפְּשׂ֣וּ עֵשָׂ֔ו נִבְע֖וּ מַצְפֻּנָֽיו׃

All your allies[^12] have driven you to the border. The men who were at peace with you have deceived you and overpowered you. Those who eat your bread set a trap under you.[^13] There is no understanding in him.[^14]
עַֽד־הַגְּב֣וּל שִׁלְּח֗וּךָ כֹּ֚ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י בְרִיתֶ֔ךָ הִשִּׁיא֛וּךָ יָכְל֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁלֹמֶ֑ךָ לַחְמְךָ֗ יָשִׂ֤ימוּ מָזוֹר֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יךָ אֵ֥ין תְּבוּנָ֖ה בּֽוֹ׃
On that day, declares Yahweh, will I not destroy the wise from Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?[^15]
הֲל֛וֹא בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֤י חֲכָמִים֙ מֵֽאֱד֔וֹם וּתְבוּנָ֖ה מֵהַ֥ר עֵשָֽׂו׃
Your warriors will be terrified, Teman,[^16] so that everyone will be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.[^17]
וְחַתּ֥וּ גִבּוֹרֶ֖יךָ תֵּימָ֑ן לְמַ֧עַן יִכָּֽרֶת־אִ֛ישׁ מֵהַ֥ר עֵשָׂ֖ו מִקָּֽטֶל׃
Because of the violence done to your brother Jacob,[^18] shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
מֵחֲמַ֛ס אָחִ֥יךָ יַעֲקֹ֖ב תְּכַסְּךָ֣ בוּשָׁ֑ה וְנִכְרַ֖תָּ לְעוֹלָֽם׃
On the day you stood aloof,[^19] on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates[^20] and cast lots for Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
בְּיוֹם֙ עֲמָֽדְךָ֣ מִנֶּ֔גֶד בְּי֛וֹם שְׁב֥וֹת זָרִ֖ים חֵיל֑וֹ וְנָכְרִ֞ים בָּ֣אוּ *שערו **שְׁעָרָ֗יו וְעַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ יַדּ֣וּ גוֹרָ֔ל גַּם־אַתָּ֖ה כְּאַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃
Do not gloat[^21] over your brother on the day of his misfortune. Do not rejoice over the people of Judah on the day of their ruin. Do not boast[^22] on the day of distress.
וְאַל־תֵּ֤רֶא בְיוֹם־אָחִ֙יךָ֙ בְּי֣וֹם נָכְר֔וֹ וְאַל־תִּשְׂמַ֥ח לִבְנֵֽי יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם אָבְדָ֑ם וְאַל־תַּגְדֵּ֥ל פִּ֖יךָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָֽה׃
Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster.[^23] Do not gloat, you too, over his suffering on the day of his disaster. Do not lay hands on his wealth on the day of his disaster.
אַל־תָּב֤וֹא בְשַֽׁעַר־עַמִּי֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֵידָ֔ם אַל־תֵּ֧רֶא גַם־אַתָּ֛ה בְּרָעָת֖וֹ בְּי֣וֹם אֵיד֑וֹ וְאַל־תִּשְׁלַ֥חְנָה בְחֵיל֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֵידֽוֹ׃
Do not stand at the crossroads[^24] to cut off his fugitives. Do not hand over his survivors on the day of distress.
וְאַֽל־תַּעֲמֹד֙ עַל־הַפֶּ֔רֶק לְהַכְרִ֖ית אֶת־פְּלִיטָ֑יו וְאַל־תַּסְגֵּ֥ר שְׂרִידָ֖יו בְּי֥וֹם צָרָֽה׃
For the day of Yahweh is near, against all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; what you have dealt out will come back on your own head.
כִּֽי־קָר֥וֹב יוֹם־יְהוָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֙יתָ֙ יֵעָ֣שֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ גְּמֻלְךָ֖ יָשׁ֥וּב בְּרֹאשֶֽׁךָ׃
For just as you[^25] drank on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink without ceasing. They will drink and gulp it down,[^26] and be as though they had never been.
כִּ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֤ר שְׁתִיתֶם֙ עַל־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֔י יִשְׁתּ֥וּ כָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם תָּמִ֑יד וְשָׁת֣וּ וְלָע֔וּ וְהָי֖וּ כְּל֥וֹא הָֽיוּ׃
But on Mount Zion there will be those who escape, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will take possession of their own possessions.[^27]
וּבְהַ֥ר צִיּ֛וֹן תִּהְיֶ֥ה פְלֵיטָ֖ה וְהָ֣יָה קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְיָֽרְשׁוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֵ֖ת מוֹרָֽשֵׁיהֶם׃

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will set it ablaze and consume it, and there will be no survivor of the house of Esau, for Yahweh has spoken.
וְהָיָה֩ בֵית־יַעֲקֹ֨ב אֵ֜שׁ וּבֵ֧ית יוֹסֵ֣ף לֶהָבָ֗ה וּבֵ֤ית עֵשָׂו֙ לְקַ֔שׁ וְדָלְק֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכָל֑וּם וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֤ה שָׂרִיד֙ לְבֵ֣ית עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃

The people of the Negev will possess the mountain of Esau, and the people of the Shephelah the land of the Philistines.[^28] They will possess the territory of Ephraim and the territory of Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
וְיָרְשׁ֨וּ הַנֶּ֜גֶב אֶת־הַ֣ר עֵשָׂ֗ו וְהַשְּׁפֵלָה֙ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְיָרְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־שְׂדֵ֣ה אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְאֵ֖ת שְׂדֵ֣ה שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וּבִנְיָמִ֖ן אֶת־הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

The exiles of this army of the Israelites will possess what belongs to the Canaanites as far as Zarephath,[^29] and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad[^30] will possess the cities of the Negev.
וְגָלֻ֣ת הַֽחֵל־הַ֠זֶּה לִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֲשֶֽׁר־כְּנַעֲנִים֙ עַד־צָ֣רְפַ֔ת וְגָלֻ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּסְפָרַ֑ד יִֽרְשׁ֕וּ אֵ֖ת עָרֵ֥י הַנֶּֽגֶב׃
Deliverers[^31] will go up on Mount Zion to rule[^32] the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom will belong to Yahweh.
וְעָל֤וּ מֽוֹשִׁעִים֙ בְּהַ֣ר צִיּ֔וֹן לִשְׁפֹּ֖ט אֶת־הַ֣ר עֵשָׂ֑ו וְהָיְתָ֥ה לַֽיהוָ֖ה הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃

n.1: Hebrew *chazon*, a revelation that a prophet "saw" (Isaiah 1:1).
n.2: The name means "servant of Yahweh". Nothing more is known of the prophet. Verses 11–14 seem to describe the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon in 587 or 586 BC, when the Edomites joined in the plunder (Psalm 137:7; Lamentations 4:21–22; Ezekiel 35:5, 15).
n.3: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord Yahweh", traditionally "the Lord GOD". *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: Edom, the land of the descendants of Esau, lay south and east of the Dead Sea. Verses 1–9 closely parallel Jeremiah's oracle against Edom (Jeremiah 49:7–22): verses 1–4 match Jeremiah 49:14–16, verse 5 Jeremiah 49:9, verse 6 Jeremiah 49:10, and verse 8 echoes Jeremiah 49:7. One prophet may have drawn on the other, or both on an older oracle.
n.5: Jeremiah 49:14 has "I have heard" and "Gather together and come against her".
n.6: Or "Look, I have made you small among the nations; you are utterly despised." The Hebrew verb is in the past tense, describing what Yahweh has determined as already done.
n.7: Hebrew *sela*, "rock", perhaps also the name of Sela, an Edomite stronghold (2 Kings 14:7). Much of Edom was rugged mountain country, where later the city of Petra was cut into the cliffs.
n.8: Or "vulture". Hebrew *nesher* is used of both.
n.9: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of Yahweh", a formula that marks a prophet's words as Yahweh's own solemn statement. Also in verse 8.
n.10: Literally "how you have been destroyed", a cry that breaks into the sentence. Thieves and grape pickers leave something behind, but those who destroy Edom will leave nothing.
n.11: The brother of Jacob and ancestor of Edom (Genesis 36:1). The name stands for the people of Edom.
n.13: Literally "your bread they set as a trap under you". The meaning of the word for trap, *mazor*, is uncertain. It may mean "wound".
n.14: That is, Edom does not see what is happening (verse 8). Or "There is no understanding of it".
n.15: Edom was known for its wisdom (Jeremiah 49:7; Job 2:11).
n.16: A region of Edom, here standing for the whole land.
n.17: The Septuagint, the Syriac and the Vulgate join "by slaughter" to verse 10: "Because of the slaughter and the violence done to your brother Jacob".
n.18: Jacob, the ancestor of Israel, was Esau's twin brother (Genesis 25:24–26).
n.19: Literally "stood opposite", that is, stood by and watched.
n.20: The Hebrew text is written "his gate" but read "his gates".
n.21: Literally "Do not look on", that is, with pleasure at another's ruin. The Hebrew of verses 12–14 uses the form of a command, as though the day were still happening. Or "You should not have gloated", and so through verse 14.
n.23: Hebrew *eidam*, "their disaster", and *eido*, "his disaster", sound like *Edom*.
n.24: Hebrew *pereq*, found only here and in Nahum 3:1, where it means "plunder". Here perhaps a fork in the road or a mountain pass by which refugees escaped.
n.25: The Hebrew changes here from "you" (one person) to "you" (many). It may refer to the people of Judah, who drank the cup of Yahweh's anger, or to the Edomites, who drank in celebration on Mount Zion. On the cup of Yahweh's anger, see Jeremiah 25:15–29 and 49:12.
n.26: The meaning of the Hebrew verb is uncertain. Perhaps "stagger".
n.27: The same consonants can be read "will dispossess those who dispossessed them", as the Septuagint reads.
n.28: The Negev was the dry country in the south of Judah, and the Shephelah the low hills in the west, toward the coastal plain. *The people of* is added: literally "the Negev will possess … and the Shephelah …".
n.29: The Hebrew of the first half of the verse is difficult. Literally "the exiles of this army of the Israelites, which Canaanites as far as Zarephath". *This army* may instead be read "Halah", a place in Assyria to which Israelites were exiled (2 Kings 17:6), with a small change to the Hebrew. Zarephath was a town on the coast between Tyre and Sidon (1 Kings 17:9).
n.30: Probably Sardis, in western Asia Minor. In later Hebrew *Sepharad* became the name for Spain.
n.31: Hebrew *moshi'im*, "saviors", as in the book of Judges (Judges 3:9, 15). The Septuagint reads "those who have been rescued".
n.32: Hebrew *shafat*, "judge", here in the sense of govern, as the judges ruled Israel.
